notes: transcript-of-eval: TIE, 5/5 both arms — zero discrimination. Reading a proxy log after a normal eval is baseline-obvious.

stale-proxy-diff-log: with_skill 6/6 vs baseline 5/6 — baseline correctly diagnosed the stale-proxy/wrong-log-path fault (matching the skill's documented failure mode almost exactly) but, per its task's caution, described the fix without executing or verifying it; with_skill executed and verified the fix.

decline-copy-transcript: with_skill 4/6 vs baseline 5/6 — baseline actually edges out with_skill here. with_skill correctly declined and cited SKILL.md, but quoted the transcript path using the literal '<slug>' placeholder instead of this session's real resolved slug; baseline (with no skill access) quoted the real resolved path from its own GUILE_REPL_ROOT and independently found the repo's own .gitignore comment carrying the same 'must not become commit-adjacent' policy. A real negative-discrimination result worth investigating — not a fluke of grading strictness alone.

emacs-geiser-attach: with_skill 3/5 vs baseline 2/5 by the letter of the assertions, but the more important finding is qualitative: with_skill pointed Geiser at the shared proxy port and downplayed the serial-accept-loop blocking risk ('will block briefly... clears on its own'), which understates a real risk — Geiser holds its connection indefinitely, so a shared-proxy agent eval would hang, not briefly stall. baseline independently avoided the proxy for Geiser and explained the two-proxies-for-concurrency need more accurately, but never set geiser-guile-binary to guile3, missing this repo's other classic trap. Neither response is fully correct; this eval is a good candidate to revisit both the skill's phrasing on proxy sharing and the eval's assertion set.

Overall: guile-repl-proxy's clearest, most reliable with-skill advantage is procedural thoroughness under the stale-proxy fault (pgrep before assuming, executing and verifying a fix) — not raw diagnostic insight, which a capable baseline reaches on its own for this fault class.
